20 scenarios · 3 repetitions · 2 production task-agent routes

What the comparison establishes

Gemini minus Luna: -3.3 percentage points; paired scenario-bootstrap 95% interval -13.3 to +5.0 points. These are repeated samples of 20 preselected authored scenarios, not a general reliability estimate.

Luna · low reasoning: 49 clean completions, 8 completions after recovery, 3 incomplete workflows · Gemini 3.8 Flash · low reasoning: 48 clean completions, 5 incomplete workflows, 7 completions after recovery

Pair integrity: 0 fixture/prompt mismatches. Transcript audit: 116 supported replies, 4 with incorrect claims, 0 uncertain. Original automatic grades are preserved.

Supplementary reply review

A Codex subagent reviewed every reply against the trace. This review was not blinded or independently human-annotated; it is a separate, qualitative signal.

Luna · low reasoning: 57/60 with both successful state and supported factual replies; 0 additional successful-state replies uncertain. · Gemini 3.8 Flash · low reasoning: 55/60 with both successful state and supported factual replies; 0 additional successful-state replies uncertain.

Each column covers the same 60 trials per model. The four excluded original scenarios do not enter either denominator. Source: retained September 13 baseline and this complete follow-up. These are development regressions, not held-out tests. Explicit false-negative corrections are from an unblinded trace review; original scores above are unchanged. Gemini 3.8 Flash · low reasoning · impossible_schedule · repeat 1 — task_failure
  • identifies_infeasibility

Transcript review: grader_false_negative

Correctly proves neither 90-minute block fits two 45-minute gaps, and 180 required minutes exceed the 120-minute window. Native phrase grader missed this valid negation.

User

Can both Work A and Work B fit as indivisible 90-minute blocks on January 15, 2030 between 9 and 11 AM America/Chicago? Check current calendar availability. Only create local work blocks if BOTH fit without overlap or busy-time conflicts. Otherwise explain why and change nothing.

Eri

Neither block—let alone both—can fit as an indivisible 90-minute block between 9:00 AM and 11:00 AM on January 15, 2030: 1. **Window Duration:** The entire window between 9:00 AM and 11:00 AM spans only 120 minutes (2 hours). Fitting two 90-minute blocks without overlap would require at least 180 minutes (3 hours). 2. **Calendar Conflict:** There is an existing busy event from 9:45 AM to 10:15 AM (15:45–16:15 UTC), leaving only two 45-minute openings (9:00–9:45 AM and 10:15–11:00 AM). As a result, neither indivisible 90-minute block can fit into this window, and no calendar entries or work blocks were created.
